rationale: This McCat 08-main sample is small (41 functions, ~8.8 KB text) with compute-oriented hot spots (trig.c, RotateMatrix, CalcObject/CalcObjectChildren), so the table favors passes with strong reverse-engineering resistance but gates the expensive ones. SUB gets low cost/risk weights and solid security/diversity weights since it is nearly free and applies broadly across the arithmetic-heavy trig and matrix code. FLA is favored with moderate penalties because flattening the larger multi-branch functions (CalcObjectChildren, CalcObject) yields the biggest control-flow hiding win at acceptable cost. BCF keeps high security/diversity weights but the highest RuntimeCost (0.8) and SizeCost (0.6) weights so the selector restricts it to functions whose features indicate low execution frequency or ample size budget, protecting the trig inner loops. SPLIT is cheap and synergistic (it feeds FLA/BCF more basic blocks to transform), so it gets a high DiversityGain weight and minimal penalties. IBR is a medium-diversity linker-level transform with modest cost, kept enabled with balanced weights. ICALL gives good indirection-based resistance but carries the highest CorrectnessRisk (0.4) in this pointer-heavy object code, so its risk weight is elevated to confine it to well-formed call sites. IGV is low-cost global-variable encoding with mild risk, kept at moderate weights to add data-level diversity cheaply. Overall the profile maximizes resistance on the large branchy functions while keeping aggregate runtime and size overhead within reason for a sub-9 KB binary.
